questions.stem: Five friends A, B, C, D, E sit in a row facing north. B is at one end. D is to the immediate right of A. C is second from the left. E is next to D. Who sits at the other end?

options.option_text: A
E
D
C

questions.explanation: TYPE 1 — pure linear. B left-end; C 2nd from left → positions: B, C, _, _, _. D to immediate right of A → AD block. E next to D → ADE. Insert: B, C, A, D, E. Other end = E.

questions.stem: P, Q, R, S, T sit in a row. T is immediately to the left of Q. R is at the right end. S is between T and P, to the immediate left of T. The leftmost person is:

options.option_text: T
P
S
Q

questions.explanation: R right-end → _ _ _ _ R. S just left of T, and between T and P → order is P, S, T. So P-S-T sit in three leftmost positions; T just left of Q → P-S-T-Q-R. Leftmost is P.

questions.stem: Six students sit in a row facing north. Veer is 3rd from the left end. Ritu is immediately to the right of Veer. Sam is at an extreme end but not near Ritu. Who could sit to the immediate left of Veer?

options.option_text: Sam
Any of the remaining three friends
Ritu
No one

questions.explanation: Veer is 3rd-from-left → position 3. Ritu at pos 4. Sam at the LEFT end (pos 1) since the right end is near Ritu's side. Pos 2 (immediate left of Veer) is any of the 3 remaining friends — information is not enough to uniquely fix.

questions.stem: In a row, A is 7th from the left and 12th from the right. The total number of persons in the row is:
questions.explanation: Formula: Total = (Left rank) + (Right rank) − 1 = 7 + 12 − 1 = 18. Subtract 1 because A is counted from both sides.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Six people sit in a row, three facing north and three facing south, with each north-facer opposite a south-facer. Therefore 'left' and 'right' for a north-facer are _____ of a south-facer.

options.option_text: Same as
Opposite to
Identical at the extremes only
Cannot be determined

questions.explanation: TYPE 2 — mixed facing. A person facing south has their back where a north-facer's front is, so their left/right are MIRRORED. This mirror rule is the single most-tested subtlety in parallel-row seating.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Seven children sit in a row. M is 3rd from the left. N is 3rd to the right of M. O is at the right end. How many children sit between N and O?
questions.explanation: M at pos 3. N = 3+3 = pos 6. O at pos 7 (right end). Positions 6 and 7 are adjacent, so 0 children sit between them. Rule: gap = |pos(A) − pos(B)| − 1.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Five engineers — Anil, Bela, Charu, Dev, Esha — sit in a row facing north. Charu sits at the rightmost seat. Anil sits immediately to the left of Charu. Bela sits 2nd from the left end. Dev does not sit adjacent to Anil. Who sits at the leftmost seat?

options.option_text: Esha is at the leftmost seat
Dev is at the leftmost seat
Bela is at the leftmost seat
Anil is at the leftmost seat

questions.explanation: Charu→5, Anil→4, Bela→2. Positions 1 and 3 remain for Dev and Esha. Anil is at position 4; its neighbours are positions 3 and 5. Since Dev cannot be adjacent to Anil, Dev ≠ 3, so Dev sits at position 1 (leftmost) and Esha at 3. Option A is wrong because Esha is placed at position 3, not position 1.

questions.stem: In a row of persons, Rahul is 8th from the left end and 13th from the right end. Five new persons then join and all sit to the right of Rahul's current position. What is Rahul's new position from the right end?

options.option_text: Rahul is now 13th from the right end
Rahul is now 18th from the right end
Rahul is now 8th from the right end
Rahul is now 15th from the right end

questions.explanation: Original row: 8 + 13 − 1 = 20 persons; 12 persons are to Rahul's right. Five new persons sit to his right, making 12 + 5 = 17 persons on his right. New rank from right = 17 + 1 = 18. Option A is wrong because it ignores the five additions entirely. Option D (15th) is a common error of adding 5 to Rahul's own left-rank instead of to the count of persons to his right.

questions.stem: Seven committee members — Harish, Inder, Jagat, Kiran, Lata, Mala, Navin — are seated in a single row. Jagat sits at one extreme end. Inder is 3rd to the right of Jagat. Kiran is immediately to the left of Mala. Harish sits between Inder and Kiran. Navin sits to the left of Lata in the two remaining positions. Who sits immediately to the right of Harish?

options.option_text: Kiran sits immediately to the right of Harish
Mala sits immediately to the right of Harish
Lata sits immediately to the right of Harish
Inder sits immediately to the right of Harish

questions.explanation: If Jagat were at position 7, Inder would need position 10 — impossible. So Jagat→1, Inder→4. For Harish to sit between Inder(4) and Kiran, Kiran must be to the right of Inder: Harish→5, Kiran→6, Mala→7. Remaining positions 2 and 3 go to Navin and Lata (Navin left): Navin→2, Lata→3. Full row: Jagat Navin Lata Inder Harish Kiran Mala. Harish's immediate right is Kiran. Option B (Mala) is wrong — Mala is at position 7, one seat beyond Kiran, not adjacent to Harish.

questions.stem: In a row of 10 persons, Usha is 4th from the left end and Vijay is 3rd from the right end. Vijay then shifts 2 places to the left. How many persons now sit between Usha and Vijay?

options.option_text: No person sits between Usha and Vijay now
Exactly 1 person sits between Usha and Vijay
Exactly 2 persons sit between Usha and Vijay
Exactly 3 persons sit between Usha and Vijay

questions.explanation: Vijay's original position from left = 10 − 3 + 1 = 8. After shifting 2 places left, Vijay is at position 6. Usha is at position 4. The only position strictly between 4 and 6 is position 5, so exactly 1 person sits between them. Option C (2 persons) is the most common error: candidates compute 6 − 4 = 2 without subtracting 1 for the 'strictly between' count.

questions.stem: Six persons — Farhan, Geeta, Hari, Ishaan, Jaya, Kavya — are seated in a row. Farhan is 2nd from the left end. Geeta is 3rd from the right end. Ishaan is immediately to the right of Geeta. Exactly two persons sit between Geeta and Hari. Kavya does not sit adjacent to Farhan. What is Jaya's position from the right end?

options.option_text: Jaya is seated 2nd from the right end
Jaya is seated 3rd from the right end
Jaya is seated 4th from the right end
Jaya is seated 5th from the right end

questions.explanation: Farhan→2; Geeta is 3rd from right in a 6-seat row = position 4; Ishaan→5. Two persons between Geeta(4) and Hari means a gap of 3: Hari at 1 or 7, so Hari→1. Remaining seats 3 and 6 for Jaya and Kavya. Kavya cannot be adjacent to Farhan(2), so Kavya ≠ 3; Kavya→6, Jaya→3. Position 3 from left in a 6-seat row = 6 − 3 + 1 = 4th from right. Option B (3rd from right) is the classic error of mistaking the left-rank for the right-rank without applying the conversion formula.

questions.stem: Nine persons P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, W, X sit in a row. P is 5th from the left end. W is at the right end. S is 2nd to the left of W. V is immediately to the right of P. Q is 3rd to the right of T. R is immediately to the left of Q. U and X fill the two remaining positions with U to the left of X. Who are the immediate left and immediate right neighbours of P, respectively?

options.option_text: Q on the immediate left and V on the immediate right
R on the immediate left and V on the immediate right
Q on the immediate left and S on the immediate right
T on the immediate left and V on the immediate right

questions.explanation: Fixed placements: P→5, W→9, S→7, V→6. Remaining slots {1,2,3,4,8} for Q,R,T,U,X. Q = T+3 and R = T+2 must all fall in this set. Testing T=1: R=3, Q=4 — both free. U and X fill {2,8}: U→2, X→8. Full row: T(1) U(2) R(3) Q(4) P(5) V(6) S(7) X(8) W(9). P's immediate left neighbour is Q(4) and immediate right is V(6). Option B is wrong because R is at position 3, two seats to the left of P, not adjacent. Option C is wrong because S is at position 7, two seats to the right of P.

questions.stem: Ten persons — A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J — sit in a row (positions 1–10, left to right). G is at the leftmost position. A is at an odd-numbered position but not at positions 1, 3, or 9. B is exactly 3 positions to the left of A. C is immediately to the right of B. F is immediately to the left of A. D is 4th from the right end. E sits adjacent to D, on the side of D toward the right end. H, I, J fill the remaining positions in that left-to-right order. Who sits immediately to the left of D?

options.option_text: H sits immediately to the left of D
A sits immediately to the left of D
F sits immediately to the left of D
I sits immediately to the left of D

questions.explanation: A is odd and not 1, 3, or 9, so A ∈ {5, 7}. If A=7: B=4, C=5, F=6; D (4th from right in 10 seats) = position 7 = A — direct conflict. So A=5, B=2, C=3, F=4. With G=1, positions {1,2,3,4,5} are filled. D = 10 − 4 + 1 = position 7; E = position 8 (adjacent to D toward right end). Remaining positions {6, 9, 10} for H, I, J in left-to-right order: H→6, I→9, J→10. D is at position 7; its immediate left is position 6 = H. Option B is wrong because A is at position 5, two seats away from D, not adjacent.
